sections.label: SIAC arbitration case numbers
sections.summary: In 2022, SIAC handled 357 new cases with parties from over 65 jurisdictions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In 2022 alone, the Singapore International Arbitration Centre (SIAC) handled 357 new cases, with parties from over 65 jurisdictions.

sections.label: Singapore Convention on Mediation
sections.summary: The Singapore Convention on Mediation was signed by more than 55 countries, highlighting commitment to amicable dispute resolution worldwide.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The Singapore Convention on Mediation, signed by more than 55 countries, highlights our commitment to promoting amicable dispute resolution worldwide.

sections.label: ITLOS model agreement
sections.summary: Singapore is the first country to have a model agreement with the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea to host its proceedings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Singapore is also the first country to have a model agreement with the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea to host its proceedings.

sections.label: Maintenance applications filed
sections.summary: In 2022, over 2,700 maintenance-related applications were filed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: In 2022, over 2,700 maintenance-related applications were filed.

sections.label: Rising online harms cases
sections.summary: With rising online harms and over 8,500 reported cases in 2023, swift protection is essential.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: With rising online harms, over 8,500 reported cases in 2023, swift protection is essential.

sections.label: New online harms agency
sections.summary: The Prime Minister announced in October last year that a new agency will be set up to deal with online harms and provide a one-stop centre for victims.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Prime Minister announced in October last year that a new agency will be set up to deal with online harms and provide a one-stop centre for victims.

sections.label: Survey on harmful online content
sections.summary: An MDDI survey found 74% of Internet users face harmful content, but only a quarter report it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: In the same month last year, a survey done by MDDI found that 74% of Internet users face harmful content, like cyberbullying or sexual content online, but only a quarter report it.

sections.label: Agency power to remove content
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the agency will have power to compel removal of harmful content.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Will the agency, for example, have the power to compel the removal of harmful content?

sections.label: CPC amendment on personal bond
sections.summary: The CPC was amended last year to require consideration of releasing persons charged with less serious offences on personal bond without a bailor.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To that end, I was very encouraged when the Criminal Procedure Code (CPC) was amended last year to expressly require the law enforcement agency or judge to consider releasing a person charged with a less serious offence on his personal bond without the need for a bailor.

sections.label: POHA Court case statistics
sections.summary: The passage asks MinLaw for updates on POHA Court cases filed and mediated, and a breakdown by harassment type.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Can MinLaw provide an update on the number of cases filed and mediated by the POHA Court; and among all the POHA cases filed, what is the breakdown of the types, that is, how many involve community neighbours; how many are online harassment; how many are sexual harassment; and how many are workplace harassment?

sections.label: Simplifying civil enforcement process
sections.summary: The passage asks MinLaw whether it intends to review civil enforcement to make recovery of monies more accessible and less painful.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: In most instances, they would still need to engage a lawyer and may sometimes still be subject to a protracted enforcement process.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: There is thus a need to simplify, expedite and better the civil enforcement process and mechanism to facilitate the victim's recovery of monies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: Can I ask MinLaw if it intends to review this and make enforcement more accessible, economical, expeditious and less painful for workers and the layman?

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Last October, I asked if MinLaw would consider simplifying enforcement of small claims and employment claims tribunals' awards.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I noted the Minister's reply that MinLaw was working on reforms, "To make the enforcement of civil judgments more effective, efficient and simpler." The challenge of enforcing awards was also recently raised in the Straits Times forum.

sections.label: Civil enforcement framework and bankruptcies
sections.summary: The Ministry said it was studying ways to improve the civil enforcement framework, and bankruptcy applications seem to have gone up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: In the Committee of Supply 2024, the Ministry mentioned it was studying ways to improve the civil enforcement framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: Perhaps, in part, because of these measures, the number of bankruptcy applications seems to have gone up.

sections.label: Community Disputes Resolution Amendment Bill passing
sections.summary: The Community Disputes Resolution (Amendment) Bill passed in November 2024, and the speaker looked forward to observing the new Community Relations Unit's effectiveness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Since then, I was heartened to see the passing of the Community Disputes Resolution (Amendment) Bill in November 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: In particular, I was looking forward to observe how effective the new Community Relations Unit (CRU) will be, with officers given investigatory and enforcement powers to intervene in neighbourly disputes.

sections.label: Community Disputes Resolution Tribunal enhanced powers
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister for an update on community mediation enhancements after the Bill's passing, hoping the Tribunal's enhanced powers quicken dispute resolution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Separately, the enhanced powers of the Community Disputes Resolution Tribunal (CDRT) will also hopefully quicken the pace of resolving community disputes effectively.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: In this context, Sir, I would like to ask the Minister to give an update on the implementation of the enhancements in the space of community mediation after the passing of the Community Disputes Resolution (Amendment) Bill.

sections.label: Copyright Act 2021 automatic IP ownership
sections.summary: Under the Copyright Act 2021, IP rights in creations automatically belong to creators even if they were paid for that work.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: Many are unaware that under the Copyright Act 2021, the IP rights in their creations automatically belong to them even if they were paid for that work.

sections.label: SMEs unaware of IP financing support
sections.summary: Many SMEs may not know about grants and financing support to unlock value from intangible assets and IP rights, which can open access to finance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: There are also many helpful grants and different areas of financing support available.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, many of our SMEs may not be aware of the opportunity to unlock value of their intangible assets and IP rights.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Successful businesses should ensure that they protect their brand value.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This may also open up avenues for access to finance.

sections.label: In-house counsels outnumber practising lawyers
sections.summary: The number of in-house counsels has outstripped the number of lawyers in practice to-date.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: The number of in-house counsels has outstripped the number of lawyers in practice to-date.

sections.label: Practice training dual seat requirement
sections.summary: Under the new practice training framework, trainee lawyers must satisfy the dual seat requirement by rotating through a solicitor's seat and a litigation seat.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
sentences.text: Under the new practice training framework, trainee lawyers must satisfy the dual seat requirement by rotating through a solicitor's seat and a litigation seat.

sections.label: SLA RSVP programme properties
sections.summary: MP asks whether RSVP properties have been awarded, how many, upcoming launches and who decides on additional properties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, since launching the Singapore Land Authority's (SLAs') Reinventing Spaces into Vibrant Places (RSVP) programme, could the Minister kindly advise whether properties have been successfully awarded and, if so, how many?

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua
sentences.text: Are there any properties scheduled for launch in the coming year and, if so, when will be the timing of this launch?

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua
sentences.text: Will the decision for additional properties under this programme be solely determined by SLA and the Urban Redevelopment Authority (URA)?

sections.label: Digital Conveyancing Portal progress
sections.summary: MP asks how the Digital Conveyancing Portal has progressed since COS 2023 and whether it is still expected by 2026.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: How has the development of the Digital Conveyancing Portal been progressing since the last update at COS 2023?

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: Is the project still expected to be completed by 2026?

sections.label: Singapore IP Strategy 2030
sections.summary: Singapore ranked fourth in WIPO's Global Innovation Index 2024, and IPOS will launch IP Management Clinics Singapore in March 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: In 2024, Singapore climbed a spot to rank fourth globally in the World Intellectual Property Organisation's (WIPO's) Global Innovation Index and remained top in Asia.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Under the Singapore IP Strategy 2030, or SIPS 2030, we are focused on spurring innovation and helping enterprises, including the smaller enterprises, unlock the value in their IA and IP.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: For businesses with overseas expansion plans, IPOS will launch the IP Management Clinics Singapore programme, in collaboration with WIPO, in March 2025.

sections.label: IPOS and VICPA MOU
sections.summary: In August 2024, IPOS signed a three-year MOU with VICPA to support the creative industry in IP education, management and capacity building.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Just last year, in August 2024, IPOS signed a three-year MOU with VICPA, to support the creative industry in IP education and management, and capacity building.

sections.label: IA valuation guidelines feedback
sections.summary: IPOS is working with partners on internationally interoperable IA valuation guidelines and will seek public feedback in the first half of 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: For enterprises looking to commercialise their IA and IP, IPOS is working with local and international partners to develop IA valuation guidelines that are interoperable internationally.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We will seek public feedback on the draft IA valuation guidelines in the first half of 2025.

sections.label: SIAC ISO 27001 certification
sections.summary: SIAC is described as the only arbitration centre with ISO 27001 Certification for its Information Security Management system.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: SIAC, as far as we know, is the only arbitration centre with ISO 27001 Certification for its Information Security Management system.

sections.label: Cross-border insolvency and simplified processes
sections.summary: Singapore adopted the UNCITRAL Model Law, clarified SICC jurisdiction for multi-jurisdiction cases, and made simplified insolvency permanent.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We have adopted the UNCITRAL Model Law on Cross-border Insolvency; and we have also clarified the SICC's jurisdiction for cases with multi-jurisdiction elements, which are particularly a feature of large cross-border restructurings.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We have introduced simplified insolvency, providing entities with simpler, faster and cheaper processes.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Members will know we first introduced this as a temporary measure during COVID-19, and this was made permanent earlier this year to benefit more companies.

sections.label: Committee on restructuring and insolvency
sections.summary: A 2023 committee on Singapore's corporate restructuring and insolvency regime consulted stakeholders and will release a report shortly.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: In 2023, some two years ago, we convened the Committee to Enhance Singapore's Corporate Restructuring and Insolvency (R&I) Regime.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The Committee has been engaged in robust debates, consulted with stakeholders, discussed the recent cases that I mentioned, as well as taken consultations on its recommendations and it will be able to release a report shortly.

sections.label: AI time savings estimate
sections.summary: A Thomson Reuters report estimated AI can save professionals up to 12 hours per week by 2029.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: For example, a Thomson Reuters report estimated that AI can save professionals up to 12 hours per week by 2029.

sections.label: Legal Technology Platform availability
sections.summary: In 2022 the Legal Technology Platform, a matter management and collaboration tool, was made available to law firms.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: In 2022, we made available the Legal Technology Platform (LTP), a matter management and collaboration tool, to law firms that desired a ready product.

sections.label: Productivity Solutions Grant for Legal Sector
sections.summary: PSG-Legal offered 70% support for up to two years, changing to 50% for one year from 1 April 2025, with over 70 applications.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We understand that sometimes the startup costs or the cost of entry into such a product could be very high.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: And so, in 2022, for example, we offered the Productivity Solutions Grant for the Legal Sector (PSG-Legal) which provided 70% support for up to two years.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: From 1 April 2025, the support level will be 50% for one year – to align with other sectors.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: To date, there are over 70 successful PSG-Legal applications from Singapore law practices, for over 400 legaltech accounts.

sections.label: Arbitration institutions expanding in Singapore
sections.summary: The Permanent Court of Arbitration is expanding in Singapore, and an MOU was signed with ICSID for its first office outside Washington DC.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: First, the Permanent Court of Arbitration, which is an intergovernmental organisation providing arbitration and other dispute resolution services, for states, is expanding its presence in Singapore, with our support.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Singapore was its first physical office in Asia and since its establishment in 2018, over the last five years, the Singapore office has until 2023 administered over 135 cases from Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Second, we have also signed an MOU with the International Centre for Settlement of Investment Disputes (ICSID) and are working towards ICSID setting up its first physical office outside its headquarters in Washington DC here in Singapore.

sections.label: Law Practices Review Committee
sections.summary: The Committee to Review the Regulatory Framework for Law Practices and Collaborations, set up in 2023, is expected to complete its work soon.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The Committee to Review the Regulatory Framework for Law Practices and Collaborations in Singapore, which we set up in 2023, is expected to complete its work soon.

sections.label: Singapore Competitiveness Ranking 2024
sections.summary: In 2024, Singapore was first in the World Competitiveness Ranking and rated top for business efficiency.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: In 2024, Singapore was first in the World Competitiveness Ranking and rated top for business efficiency.

sections.label: Civil Judgment Enforcement Measures
sections.summary: Feedback said enforcement costs can be disproportionate to judgment sums; the Court will get greater powers and new Civil Judgment Enforcement Officers will be created.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We received feedback that the time, effort and costs – Mr Tay spoke about that – of enforcing judgments can sometimes be disproportionate to the judgment sum.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We are looking to address these areas by providing the Court with greater powers to identify the assets and income streams of the judgment debtor as well as introducing new modes of enforcement to deter and punish non-compliance with Court orders.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We will also create new Civil Judgment Enforcement Officers, who will effectively assist litigants who wish to enforce their civil judgments.

sections.label: PDO Applications in 2024
sections.summary: In 2024, PDO received almost 1,900 applications and about 1,000 were assessed as eligible.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: In 2024, PDO received almost 1,900 applications and about 1,000 were assessed as eligible.

sections.label: Community Relations Unit Pilot Tampines
sections.summary: The Community Relations Unit pilot, including directed mediation for severe noise and hoarding cases, will start in Tampines from the second quarter of this year.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The Community Relations Unit (CRU) pilot, including directed mediation, for severe noise and hoarding cases will start in Tampines from the second quarter of this year.

sections.label: Satellite Mediation Locations Increase
sections.summary: CMC has increased the number of satellite mediation locations from 10 in 2023 to 18 in 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: CMC has also increased the number of satellite mediation locations from 10 in 2023 to 18 in 2025.

sections.label: State properties for senior living
sections.summary: SLA activated state properties for older Singaporeans' independent living and plans a tender for 20 heritage properties at Admiralty Road East for multi-generational co-living.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: First, to address rising demand for independent living for older Singaporeans, SLA activated state properties, such as 79 to 95 Hindoo Road, 26 Evans Road and 98 Henderson Road.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: Building on the response, SLA plans to launch a tender in the first quarter of this year for 20 heritage properties at Admiralty Road East for multi-generational co-living.

sections.label: Consultants tender for alteration works
sections.summary: SLA called a tender in September 2024 for a multidisciplinary team of consultants for Additions and Alteration works, with estimated completion in 2028.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: SLA called a tender for a multidisciplinary team of consultants in September 2024 to provide consultancy services for Additions and Alteration works, with estimated completion in 2028.

sections.label: DCP private residential resale transactions
sections.summary: The first phase of the DCP focuses on private residential resale transactions, with live OTP transactions targeted to commence as a pilot initially in 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: The first phase of the DCP focuses on private residential resale transactions, which make up more than half of private real estate transactions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: Live OTP transactions for the private residential resale market is targeted to commence as a pilot initially in 2025.

sections.label: Guidelines for Gen AI legal use
sections.summary: MinLaw is working on guidelines to guide legal professionals to be smart buyers and users of Gen AI tools, encouraging safe and responsible use.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: Legal professionals should use Gen AI tools safely and responsibly, even as we encourage its adoption.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: Considering this context, MinLaw is working on guidelines to guide legal professionals to be smart buyers and users of Gen AI tools.

sections.label: New legislation on three buckets
sections.summary: MinLaw and MDDI are working together on new legislation that will cover three broad buckets.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: To address these gaps, MinLaw and MDDI are working together on new legislation that will cover three broad buckets.

sections.label: Protection order applications and personal bond
sections.summary: The passage gives PHC protection order application numbers and harassment breakdowns from 2021 to 2024, and notes a 2024 amendment allowing personal bond for certain non-bailable offences.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: The number of applications for protection orders to the PHC since it started operations on 1 June 2021 are as follows: (a) 346 PO applications were filed in 2021; (b) 520 in 2022, (c) 526 in 2023; and (d) 631 in 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: In terms of breakdown, out of the 2,023 PO applications filed from 1 June 2021, which is when the PHC commenced operations, to 31 December 2024, there were complaints about the following kinds of harassments: (a) 760 cases involved cyberbullying; (b) 719 cases involved doxing; (c) 485 cases involved workplace harassment; (d) 253 cases involved sexual harassment; and (e) 122 cases involved harassment by debt collectors, moneylenders or creditors.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: The total number is 2,339, though there were 2,023 applications, because a single application can contain complaints for about more than one type of harassment.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: I now turn to Ms Sylvia Lim's query on the personal bond in criminal cases – an amendment in the Criminal Procedure (Miscellaneous Amendments) Act 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: This allows persons accused of non-bailable offences punishable with up to seven years' imprisonment to be released on personal bond, as an alternative to bail.

sections.label: Personal bond for non-bailable offences
sections.summary: Since the amendment was implemented in August 2024, more than 100 accused persons have been released on personal bond for non-bailable offences.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: Since the amendment was implemented in August 2024, more than 100 accused persons have been released on personal bond for non-bailable offences.

sections.label: First-stop legal information portal
sections.summary: Launched in March last year, this first-stop portal consolidates access to legal information, legal services and law awareness resources.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: Launched in March last year, this is a first-stop portal that consolidates access to legal information, legal services and law awareness resources.

sections.label: Business-friendly legal framework
sections.summary: He spoke about growing the economy and strengthening the legal framework to be business-friendly in IP, dispute resolution and debt restructuring and insolvency.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: He also spoke about our efforts and approach to growing the economy, even as Singapore faces challenges in this turbulent external environment.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: We will strengthen our legal framework to be business-friendly and forward-looking, especially in the areas of IP, dispute resolution and debt restructuring and insolvency.

sections.label: Clamping down on debt consultancy firms
sections.summary: Some debtors end up in bigger debt after consulting such firms, so steps will be taken to clamp down on these practices and raise awareness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The irony is that some debtors consult with these firms only to find that they end up in a bigger hole, a larger debt, as a consequence of trying to find a solution to their debt.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So, we are very mindful of this and we will take steps to look at how we can have levers to clamp down on such practices by these firms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Indeed, it is also true, Sir, as Mr Zhulkarnain points out, that public awareness is key, to paraphrase him.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We will step up significantly on steps to raise awareness and we will do this in a few ways.

sections.label: Guide for bankruptcy applications
sections.summary: A guide will be published to help debtors submitting bankruptcy applications and turn them away from relying on debt consultancy firms for paperwork.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Second, we intend to also publish a guide to help debtors along the journey of submitting bankruptcy applications, and teach them and guide them on what steps to take, to try to turn them away from having to rely on such debt consultancy firms to get assistance for the paperwork.

sections.label: Questions on personal bond figures
sections.summary: He asked for confirmation that the figure of about 100 persons released on personal bond is combined from law enforcement and the Courts.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: Earlier, he mentioned that under the new provisions that were effective on 1 August, about 100 persons had been released on personal bond instead of on bail.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: I would like him to confirm that this is actually the combined number from law enforcement, as well as the Courts.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: And the second question is if that is the case, this means that if it is 100 persons over six months, it is only about 16 persons per month, which to me is quite a low figure.
